pages.heading: The Wreck of the 1873 and Brennen
paragraphs: Gather 'round the campfire, young’uns, and let me tell you a tale about the West you won't find in any history book. You’ve heard of Wyatt Earp and Buffalo Bill, but have you heard of the Awesome Aussie Possum Posse?

Back in 1873, a ship full of exotic animals from Australia was heading for a brand-new zoo in Philadelphia. But a monster storm hit the Pacific, and that ship smashed right into the rocks off the California coast!

Amidst the crashing waves, a bushy-tailed young possum named Brennen wrestled his cage door open just as the ocean swallowed the vessel. He tumbled through the rapids and woke up gasping on a sandy beach.

He wasn't alone, though. The shore was littered with crates and screaming animals trying to dodge the greedy poachers who wanted to lock ‘em back up. It was a life-and-death situation, and the adventure was just starting!

pages.heading: Pygmy's Great Escape
paragraphs: Brennen was a brave soul, but he was feeling pretty low until he heard a muffled voice calling from the sand. He found a small hand poking out like a leaping lizard and pulled with all his might!

After digging through the sand and popping the crate’s latch, he expected a frantic thanks. Instead, a portly little fellow calmly mozied out. He picked up a shipping label, read, "Oh, apparently I'm Pygmy, Pygmy Possum," and just tossed it away like trash.

Brennen reached out for a hand, but Pygmy had other ideas. Quick as a whip, Pygmy wrapped a tail the size of a city square around Brennen’s arm and catapulted him clear across the beach! Brennen landed headfirst in the sand, bells ringing in his ears, realizing he’d just met a very unusual—and very strong—new partner.

pages.heading: Gretel and the Goon
paragraphs: While Brennen was still shaking the sand out of his fur, he saw a "dazzling damsel" in trouble. He decided to be the hero and bit a poacher’s ankle to set her free.
Well, the poacher wasn't too happy and snatched Brennen up in a crushing fist! Brennen thought he was saving her, but this lady didn't need no knight in shining armor.
She looked at him, puckered her face, and scoffed, "Oh, you're rescuing me?" Then she bit the captor’s hand herself! As she dropped, she spread her arms to reveal sleek gliding membranes.

"Crickey, you're a glider!" Brennen shouted as she caught the wind. She introduced herself as Gretel the Greatest Greater Glider and soared away, leaving poor Brennen staring down a very grumpy, grunting goon.

pages.heading: Remy’s Giggling Rescue
paragraphs: Now, Brennen was in a real pickle, staring right into the gruesome gaze of that poacher. He was about to meet his end when, out of thin air, another possum appeared!
This new fellow plopped perfectly onto the goon’s... well, let’s just say he hit the goon right where it hurts.
The poacher let out a shriek and fell to the floor, letting Brennen wiggle free.
The newcomer was a googly-eyed ringtail named Remy Rodrick, and he was giggling up a storm! He told Brennen he’d never met the goon before, but he saw he was giving him big trouble.
Brennen tried to act debonair, dusting himself off and acting like he had it all under control, but he knew he owed Remy a big one.
The two shook hands, finally safe for a fleeting moment.

pages.heading: Willow's Charging Welcome
paragraphs: They didn't have long to celebrate. A wild, white possum came charging in, hotter than a jalapeno in hot sauce!
This was Willow Willamena, and she was fuming. She called Brennen a "brash-brained bogan" because he’d been shouting counter-orders while she was trying to save the animals.
She was so mad she put up her fists, ready for a Texas tango right there on the sand!
Brennen shouted back, calling her an imbecile for wanting to lead everyone into a "lion's den" of a tree hollow.
It looked like they were going to scrap until Remy stepped in. He grabbed Willow’s fist and started shaking it like they were old friends, introducing himself with a grin.
Behind Willow was a sweet little honey possum named Hanna Holly, who just nodded along. This was one prickly bunch of heroes!

pages.heading: Hanna’s Desert Tea
paragraphs: The group took off into the Southern California desert to escape the poachers, but that sun was hotter than a steam engine in Hades.

Gretel and Pygmy passed right out from the heat. Willow was sure they were doomed because there wasn't a drop of water in sight. But little Hanna Holly just smiled. With a bit of creativity, she went to work on an agave bush, moving so fast she looked like she was everywhere at once!
In seconds, she’d fashioned chairs, an awning, and tiny cups filled with a thick white liquid. The others were flabbergasted as they sat in agave chairs and sipped on "Hanna’s Desert Tea."
Remy even said it was better than Tasmanian Pepper Berries! They were finally relaxing when the ground began to rumble like a giant’s belly ache.

pages.heading: Stampeding Plaid and Steeds
paragraphs: A stampede of bighorn sheep was heading straight for them! Willow and Brennen shouted different orders again—one said "run" and the other said "take cover."
The rest of the possums got so confused they ended up in a tangled pile with Pygmy's tail roped all around them! But the sheep stopped just a skunk’s hair away.
Standing atop the biggest ram was a mysterious striped possum. He shimmied down and started gulping down Hanna’s tea without saying a word.
When Willow asked his name, he just grunted, "Plaid." He was a man of few words—mostly just "yep" and "nope."
He’d been riding those sheep like they were ponies! Pygmy suggested they all use the sheep to ride into town, and even though Willow tried to act like it was her idea, the plan was set.

pages.heading: Rough Start to a Great Adventure
paragraphs: The Posse was finally moving out, but not everyone was a natural rider.

Brennen and Willow led the way on big rams, racing toward a town called Hang Town. Remy, Gretel, and Plaid followed close behind. But poor Pygmy had to lasso a jackrabbit and was barely hanging on as it hopped away!  And Hanna? She built a whole stagecoach out of tumbleweeds and agave leaves, hitched to two kangaroo rats named Ranga and Koo.

The gang were headed east to save their friends from the zoo. Can these seven unlikely heroes stop bickering long enough to survive the Wild West? Can they cross the entire United State to rescue their friends from the Philadelphia Zoo ? Will thye actually make it back to Australia ?
Here's hoping!
